title: Experts worry about Nvidia's AI chip sales in China and influence over Trump
gist: While the Trump-Xi summit produced no AI or export-control progress, China is weighing letting Alibaba and ByteDance import possibly millions of Nvidia RTX Pro 5500 gaming chips for AI servers, with ByteDance planning a 1 million chip order worth two quarters of projected Nvidia sales. Critics say Jensen Huang has become Trump's most influential tech adviser, steering him to downplay AI risks and loosen chip controls.

insights.claim: China is considering relaxing controls to let its biggest AI firms import perhaps millions more banned Nvidia chips over the next year, with MIIT asking Alibaba and ByteDance for plans to buy RTX Pro 5500 chips.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
entities: Ministry of Industry and Information Technology
insights.so_what: Reopening China could restore a major revenue stream for Nvidia.

insights.claim: If China approves, ByteDance plans to order 1 million chips, which would secure two quarters of Nvidia's projected sales, and Nvidia is reportedly preparing to ship first orders in December.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: A concrete upside catalyst for Nvidia's China revenue.

insights.claim: Huang has blamed US export controls for cutting Nvidia's share of China's advanced AI chip market from about 95% to zero, and delayed H200 approvals left China sales below 1% of Nvidia's data center revenue last quarter.
insights.speaker: Ashley Belanger
insights.so_what: Nvidia's current estimates contain little China revenue, so any reopening is incremental upside.
